do_not_touch.reason: Shared across every encounter set. Repointing it to the Korean 6x5 back would give its Midwinter targets the wrong back and, if done by path-wide substitution, corrupt the entire mod. Only 2 of its files sit inside Korean-PlayerCards.KoreanI, which is what shows its targets live almost entirely in Campaigns.
Shared mod-wide; 814 of its files sit inside Korean-PlayerCards.KoreanI alone. Only 15 belong to Midwinter targets, so a directory-wide back rewrite would hit 799 unrelated cards.

atlas_urls.note: korean_url values are copied from upload-map.json, the output of an upload the tool verified with head_object + a browser-UA public GET, and re-verified independently (verify-r2.json) with a full-body sha256 round-trip. They are NOT copied from recompose-upload-manifest.json.face_url, which holds pre-upload predictions.

scope.forbidden_reason: English base data. The 8x5 face URL alone occurs in 116 files: 36 in the langpack (the targets) and 80 in these two trees (40 each). A repo-wide substitution Koreanizes the English scenario, widens the fork's changed-path set vs upstream/main, and creates a permanent overlap-gate liability for the nightly rebase.
scope.forbidden_tool: SCED-tools/scripts/apply-atlas-faceurls.py - it repacks cards onto new cells and rewrites CardID and the CustomDeck key in lockstep, and it consumes an atlas_manifest.json + mapping.json pair whose schema is deliberately incompatible with recompose-upload-manifest.json. :315 and :316 are hand-edits.
invariants: only the FaceURL and BackURL string values change
scope.object_filter: NONE. The selector is the URL predicate alone, over EVERY object under allowed_paths regardless of its Name. Korean-PlayerCards.KoreanI holds 1945 Card and 191 CardCustom objects and CardCustom carries CustomDeck.<k>.FaceURL identically, so filtering by Name would hide a future target from both the edit and the count meant to catch it. observed_object_names records what was actually seen and is asserted, not used to filter. The Custom_PDF guide object is excluded automatically because it has no CustomDeck; no Deck container object exists under either allowed path. Container Deck objects carrying a target URL exist only in the English base trees, which forbidden_paths already excludes (measured: 8 per tree, 16 in total, alongside 72 Card per tree).
scope.selector: objects under allowed_paths whose CustomDeck.<k>.FaceURL equals an english_url in substitutions[] where side == face

substitutions.note: 27 objects for 26 arkham_ids: 71033 Silver Twilight Lodge has two independent TTS objects (4a2568 Factions, ccce29 Rivals). Matching on URL covers both; matching on card-text-en.json's 46 Campaigns cards would miss ccce29. observed_deck_keys is EVIDENCE, never an input - deck_key is never rewritten.
Consumed by BOTH :315 (20 Campaigns objects) and :316 (16 Player Cards objects). :317 asserts this URL is byte-identical across the two packs.

The ONLY back that moves. Midwinter-specific. Its english_url lives at card-text-en.json's top-level shared_back_6x5 key, NOT under sheets - a loop over sheets drops this entry entirely. Its objects are exactly the S1 objects.

sweep_2026_08_24.note: The first post-suppression sweep of the whole corpus, run for design 6 step 8's calibration. Recorded here because it is the negative evidence data/layouts/midwinter.json's calibrated_from is derived from, and because 86 of 86 non-defect faces firing at a flat 34 is the measurement that made a per-group threshold necessary rather than merely preferable. See data/layouts/README.md.
sweep_2026_08_24.resweep_note: Re-swept 2026-08-24 after the measure_bands() fix. The zero groups are NOT a plate artifact: only 10 of 88 faces changed clearance at all, and in every remaining zero group the floor is set by a band that genuinely reaches the window's trailing edge. Per design 5.5 those are findings for step 16's adjudication, not threshold problems.

provenance.note: THE REFERENCE RECEIPT, backfilled. Midwinter shipped before koreanize existed, so no stage wrote this file at the time; it is reconstructed from the artifacts that DO survive -- the three git commits that made the repository writes, and the corpus' own atlas-urls.json -- so that the receipt tier has a worked example and step 15's `golden` has something to compare against.
provenance.write_set_from: git log over SCED-downloads; one row per path, pre_sha256 taken at the FIRST commit's parent and post_sha256 at the LAST commit that touched it, so a path written twice is one row spanning both.
